target_paper_title: QSVD: Efficient Low-rank Approximation for Unified Query-Key-Value Weight Compression in Low-Precision Vision-Language Models

gold_annotations.topic: This paper studies efficient compression of vision-language models, focusing on reducing attention-side compute, parameter storage, and KV-cache cost during inference. The setting is low-precision VLM deployment, where both low-rank approximation and post-training quantization are used to keep multimodal models accurate while making them cheaper to run on constrained hardware.
gold_annotations.golden_gap: The paper argues that existing efficient VLM and LLM compression methods address only parts of the problem. Prior attention variants such as grouped-query, multi-query, and latent attention reduce KV-related cost, while prior SVD methods mainly compress weights or compress K and V separately, and prior VLM quantization methods do not combine quantization with SVD in a unified way. According to the paper, this leaves a gap for a method that jointly compresses query, key, and value projections, allocates rank according to their actual effect on VLM accuracy, and remains compatible with low-bit quantization despite severe activation outliers in multimodal models.
gold_annotations.golden_method: The proposed method is QSVD. It first concatenates the query, key, and value weight matrices into a single joint QKV matrix and applies low-rank SVD so that Q, K, and V share one down-projection and keep separate up-projections. This reduces weight size, FLOPs, and buffered intermediate cache relative to separate per-matrix decompositions. The paper then introduces a cross-layer rank allocation strategy that scores each singular value by estimating the loss increase caused by truncating it, using calibration-data gradients and a memory-efficient importance-score formula. On top of the low-rank model, QSVD applies post-training quantization to weights and activations, using rotation-based outlier smoothing and a learnable beta parameter to suppress outliers in the intermediate low-rank representation, enabling low-precision inference for the compressed VLM.
gold_annotations.gold_experiment: The experiments evaluate QSVD on five VLMs: LLaVA-v1.5 7B, LLaVA-v1.5 13B, LLaVA-Next 7B, LLaVA-Next 13B, and SmolVLM-Instruct. Calibration uses 256 ScienceQA training samples. The main evaluation benchmarks are ScienceQA, VizWiz, and SEED-Bench-IMG, with results reported through VLMEvalKit on NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPUs. The paper first compares an SVD-only variant, QSVD-noQ, against ASVD and SVD-LLM under matched hardware ratios R1 and R2, then compares quantized QSVD against DuQuant, QVLM, and QASVD under W8A8, W8A4, and W4A4 settings. It also includes ablations on rank allocation versus uniform-rank and Fisher-based schemes, the effect of learning beta, long-sequence evaluation on HRBench-4K, hallucination evaluation on HallusionBench, and latency measurements on an RTX 4070 with 4K token length. The paper reports that QSVD generally achieves the best accuracy-hardware tradeoff, can approach FP16 performance with much smaller cache ratios, improves groundedness metrics, and reaches up to 13.1x speedup in the reported latency setup.
